Game Concept: STARSTRUCK: Fashion Frenzy

A multiplayer fashion runway game inspired by the social competition and styling gameplay of Dress to Impress and It Girl, but with its own identity, features, and progression.

Genre

Multiplayer Fashion 

Social Roleplay 

Runway Competition 

Dress-Up 

Life Simulation 

Target Players

Ages 9+ 

Friends 

Fashion lovers 

Casual and competitive players 

Story

You arrive in Star City, the world's biggest fashion capital. Every day, famous designers host themed fashion shows where models compete for trophies, fame, exclusive clothing, and luxury apartments.

Become the next global fashion icon by winning competitions, building your wardrobe, and collecting rare outfits.

Gameplay Loop

Join server 

Theme appears 

Shop for clothing 

Customize body, hair, makeup, accessories 

Pose on runway 

Players vote 

Winners receive rewards 

Unlock more fashion items 

Repeat

Anti-Cheat & Fair Play

Outfit plagiarism detection that highlights nearly identical submissions. 

Automatic filtering for inappropriate outfit names or chat. 

AFK detection to prevent inactive players from winning rewards. 

Vote balancing to reduce unfair group voting. 

Unique Features

Designer Studio: Create clothing using unlocked patterns, fabrics, and decals to build your own fashion collections. 

Trend Meter: Each day, featured colors, styles, or accessories give a small score bonus when used creatively. 

Fashion Magazine: Winning outfits may appear on a weekly in-game magazine cover. 

Photo Studio: Take high-quality screenshots with custom lighting, backgrounds, and poses. 

Team Runways: Compete in pairs or teams to create coordinated outfits. 

Fashion Academy: Complete tutorials and style challenges to unlock advanced customization options. 

Style Seasons: A seasonal progression system with free and premium reward tracks featuring exclusive cosmetics. 

This concept captures the appeal of runway fashion games while adding original progression, social features, creative tools, and customization systems to establish its own identity rather than copying existing games.

answers.ask: Which of the ten maps should be built first, and do they all reuse one runway layout or is each map its own?
answers.answer: Build Luxury Mall first as the core launch map. Each map should be its own themed environment, while using the same standard runway gameplay layout for a smaller, consistent first build.

answers.ask: How many players per server? Runway length and lobby capacity both depend on it.
answers.answer: Use 10 players per server, keeping the runway show manageable while everyone receives their 20-second turn. The lobby should comfortably hold those 10 players.

answers.ask: Are the apartments part of the same map or a separate instanced space?
answers.answer: Apartments should be separate instanced spaces so home decorating and friend visits do not interfere with active fashion-show rounds.

scene_prompt: Create the core 3D launch map for a multiplayer fashion runway game: a Luxury Mall themed environment for 10 players. Arrange a comfortable central lobby that holds all players, with a standard runway-show layout featuring a long catwalk, model entrance, audience/viewing area, and a top-three winners’ podium. Surround the show space with mall shopping and styling zones for clothing, body, hair, makeup, accessories, and shoes, plus a designer studio and photo studio. Luxury apartments are separate instanced home spaces, not part of the active mall map. Future maps are distinct themed environments but reuse this consistent runway layout.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Roleplay & Avatar Sim, specifically a multiplayer dress-up runway experience. Its social styling and avatar-customization loop make `stage-runway` the governing form rather than a generic party stage.

### Shape and preset
Use `stage-runway`: a fashion-show stage whose catwalk, audience orientation, and preparation spaces organize the whole Luxury Mall. Match the Dress Up preset, retaining its social gathering and photographic presentation priorities. The requested mall retail and styling rooms expand that preset without changing its runway-led shape.

### Config requirements
Use `social-hub` as visible geometry: a comfortable central mall lobby sized for all 10 players to gather before and between shows. Use `vignette-photo` as visible geometry: the photo studio is a deliberately lit, composed fashion-photo set, with additional polished mall backdrops where useful. No invisible layout options are required. The separately instanced luxury apartments are explicitly outside this active mall map and are not rendered here.

### Layout components
Build one indoor Luxury Mall launch map. Place the central lobby as a broad arrival and gathering zone at the front, comfortably holding 10 players. Beyond it, make the runway-show hall the dominant central zone: a long straight catwalk runs from a screened model entrance at one end toward a top-three winners’ podium at the other, with a broad audience/viewing area aligned along the catwalk sides and facing its presentation direction.

Wrap the show hall with connected mall storefront-style styling zones: distinct clothing, body-customization, hair, makeup, accessories, and shoes areas. Place the designer studio on one side as a creative workshop-like retail space, and the photo studio on the opposite side as a contained glamorous shooting set. Use wide indoor mall corridors to connect lobby, shops, studios, and runway hall without forcing passage through the catwalk. The boundary is the enclosing luxury-mall architecture: polished floors, storefront glazing, display windows, warm ceiling lighting, and elegant walls. Frame the map as a readable indoor plan with the runway as the visual spine and the lobby foreground.

### Render order
Use `isometric`: the visual identity, luxury finishes, runway spectacle, and composed audience-facing stage are authoritative; this is not a topology-sensitive course requiring a plan-first generation pass.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium, driven by a 10-player lobby, full runway hall, six styling retail zones, and two studios within one mall. Theme: glossy upscale fashion mall, contemporary luxury, warm lighting, polished stone and glass, editorial glamour. Use `P0`; the map is one contiguous indoor surface with no forced overhang, exterior-to-interior transition, separate active maps, or validation-critical route.
